bib.title: SCALING LAWS FOR GENERATIVE MIXED-MODAL LANGUAGE MODELS

question: How do loss, model size and data size scale for generative models over tokens from several modalities, and when does competition between modalities turn into synergy?
hypothesis: Adding an additive interaction term (competition or synergy) to the Chinchilla uni-modal scaling law predicts the scale at which two modalities stop competing.
contributions: We develop neural scaling laws for mixed-modalities models that include text, speech, images, code, and their numerous couplings.
We discover a set of scaling laws describing the competition between arbitrary modalities.
We provide a simple recipe for selecting hyper-parameters in a multi-modal setting when optimal uni-modal hyper-parameters are known.

We uncover correlations between the scaling laws parameters we propose and various training phenomena, including training stability, optimal batch size, and coordinate ascent-like behavior in the optimization process across different modalities.

method.summary: Decoder-only causally-masked transformers (8M to 30B) are trained on tokenised text, image, image-text, speech, speech-text, code and molecule data, one epoch each. Chinchilla-form laws are fit per modality and per pair (50% of tokens each) with an added interaction term, then used to predict the compute-optimal point where Speech|Text stops competing, which is tested with a 30B run.
method.task: next-token (causally masked) pretraining on mixed-modal token sequences; scaling-law fitting

datasets.name: Image
datasets.source: custom subset of Schuhmann et al. (2022) plus custom image-text set scraped from Common Crawl
datasets.preprocessing: Make-A-Scene tokenizer, 1024 tokens per image from 8192 vocab; NSFW and watermarked images removed; no captions

datasets.name: Speech
datasets.source: custom web-mined unlabeled podcasts/news plus LibriSpeech, CommonVoice, VoxPopuli, Spotify Podcast, People's Speech
datasets.preprocessing: music and sensitive speech removed; LangID to keep English only; HuBERT units, K-means codebook 2000

datasets.name: Speech-Text
datasets.source: ASR and TTS data from Multilingual LibriSpeech and VoxPopuli

datasets.name: Molecules
datasets.source: SMILES from Zinc dataset prepared by Chilingaryan et al. (2022)

models.name: OPT/GPT-3-style decoder-only family 8M-6.7B
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, pre-norm, ReLU, learned positional encodings, causal masked objective
models.init_from: normal mean 0 std 0.006 truncated at two std (Megatron-LM variant)
models.tokenizer: unified BPE trained on 10 million sentences sampled across datasets; image and speech tokens one token each; digit splitting
models.vocab: inferred: 2^16 (text printed as 'vocab size of 216', superscript lost)

models.name: HuBERT BASE (speech tokenizer)
models.architecture: conv encoder + 12 layer transformer, dim 768, FFN 3072, 12 heads

other.pretraining: 32 GPUs, three iterations, 400K updates each, 221K hours unlabeled speech in eight languages

training.objective: causal masked objective (CM3, Aghajanyan et al. 2022); causal LM ablation in A.2 gives near-identical fit parameters
training.optimizer: Adam, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98; gradient clipping max norm 1.0
training.lr_schedule: polynomial decay (MetaSeq), end LR 10% of peak
training.batch_size: 1M tokens (Table 2); batch-size study 0.5M(text only), 1M, 2M, 4M, 8M over 5B tokens
training.steps: inferred: about 100000 updates at 100B tokens (Fig 1 axis)
training.tokens: uni-modal and bi-modal grid 5B, 10B, 100B; 30B Speech|Text run 50B tokens
training.regularisation: restart policy: if training perplexity does not decrease after 500 million tokens, restart with LR reduced by factor 0.8
training.hardware: cluster of 768 80GB A100 GPUs; most experiments 64 GPUs at a time
training.wall_clock: all experiments within a two-month time frame

other.framework: metaseq, PyTorch, fairscale FSDP, Megatron-LM tensor parallelism
other.bi_modal_pairs: Image-Text|Code, Image-Text|Speech-Text, Image-Text|Text, Speech|Text, Code|Text, Molecule|Code, Speech|Code
other.hyperparameters: same as uni-modal runs for bi-modal

metrics.name: perplexity (PPL)
metrics.definition: standard perplexity on held-out data per modality; scaling laws fit to loss

metrics.name: R-FID / Accuracy@1 (image tokenizer)
metrics.definition: FID of reconstructed ImageNet validation images; ImageNet classifier accuracy on reconstructions

metrics.name: WER (speech tokenizer)
metrics.definition: word error rate of pretrained ASR on original vs HuBERT-reconstructed audio

baselines: independent uni-modal models on the same per-modality tokens (0.5*[L(N,Di)+L(N,Dj)])
eval.protocol: Fit seven parameters per modality by minimising Huber(delta=0.03) of LSE residuals with L-BFGS over a grid of initialisations, following Hoffmann et al. (2022); Huber delta higher than Chinchilla's. Fit on 8M-6.7B, tested at 30B. No seeds or error bars reported.

limits: Fitted laws cover only seven pairs of modalities chosen for variety; the authors say an exhaustive sweep was infeasible for computational reasons.
Fits use models up to 6.7B; only one extrapolation test (30B Speech|Text, 50B tokens), one run per size, no seeds or error bars.
Single epoch of training only; all results are perplexity, no downstream task evaluation.
Emergent-phenomenon correlations are shown in figures with no coefficients and are called potentially worthy of study in future work.
Dataset sizes for Speech, Speech-Text, Code, Molecules not stated; the Huber delta had to be raised for generalisation to held-out data.
Competition and synergy are defined at a 50/50 token mix; other mixes not studied.
Text law coefficients differ from Chinchilla because a different dataset is used.

terms.definition: when both sides of the inequality are equal (C_ij equals the competition terms in function approximation and optimisation)
two modalities performing better than two individual models trained on the same number of per-modality tokens; formally C_ij > A_ij/N^alpha_ij + B_ij/(|Di|+|Dj|)^beta_ij
the empirical phenomena of two modalities performing worse than if we trained two individual models on the same number of per-modality tokens
empirical modality definition by perplexity of one dataset under another's model; sigma=3 gives seven modalities
